steps.name: Sample structure QC: library sizes, PCA, sample distances, low-depth sample verdict
caveats: A library size ~4x below median gives sample_01 a wider effective confidence interval in any later DE model via its size factor — that is expected model behavior, not evidence to remove it

Do not conflate low depth with poor RNA quality or mislabeling; the PCA/distance-heatmap clustering behavior of sample_01 relative to its condition group is the deciding evidence for the verdict, not the library size number alone

With only 12000 genes profiled (likely already a curated/filtered gene set rather than a full ~20k+ human transcriptome), the top-500-variable-gene PCA still applies but note this gene-count context when interpreting variance explained
steps.context: Data context: /eval-full-32-with-qc-only-n6-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 13 columns = gene symbol + 12 samples, raw integer Salmon gene-level counts) and /eval-full-32-with-qc-only-n6-2/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample id, condition). Design: 6 AD lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Known caveat from the data profile: sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median of the cohort. This is a pure exploratory QC step — no hypothesis test, no condition-based (non-blind) transformation, and no gene filtering beyond the standard DESeq2 low-count pre-filter, since the model design should not bias this unbiased structural view.
steps.question: For the 12 skin samples (6 AD lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts over 12000 genes), what are the per-sample library sizes, how do samples separate on PCA of the top 500 variable genes after a blind VST, what do the sample-to-sample Euclidean distances show, and specifically — does sample_01 (flagged with a library size ~4x below the cohort median) look like an outlier or does it cluster normally with its condition group?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC (blind vst, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) per R-0033@40bf; low-depth sample sample_01 kept, inspected, and reported with a stated keep/exclude reason per R-0008@440d, not dropped by default

constraints: Use vst(..., blind=TRUE) — QC must not use the design formula so the transform does not bake in the condition contrast before it is examined
Pre-filter genes to >=10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smaller group size) before vst, consistent with standard DESeq2 practice — do not filter more aggressively
Do NOT silently drop sample_01 or any other sample; it must appear in every plot and in the library-size table with condition label
PCA must be computed on the top 500 highest-variance genes (rank by row variance of the vst-transformed matrix) as standard practice, not all 12000 genes

State the verdict on sample_01 explicitly as text output, referencing its position in both the PCA and the distance heatmap, and give a specific keep/exclude recommendation with the reason — depth alone is not sufficient reason to exclude per DESeq2 size-factor normalization behavior
acceptance_criteria: Bar plot or table of raw library size (total counts) per sample, all 12 samples labeled by condition, with sample_01 and the cohort median annotated
DESeq2 vst(blind=TRUE) computed on the full filtered count matrix (pre-filter: genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples, the smaller group size)
PCA plot (PC1 vs PC2 at minimum, with % variance explained) on the top 500 most-variable genes from the vst matrix, points colored by condition (lesional vs control) and labeled by sample ID
Sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap (12x12) on the vst matrix, annotated by condition, with hierarchical clustering
Explicit reporting of sample_01's library size and detected-gene count (genes with count>0) alongside the other 11 samples

A stated verdict on sample_01: whether it clusters with its condition group on PCA/distance heatmap or departs as an outlier, and a recommendation (keep for DE with the caveat that its size factor will down-weight it, or exclude with a stated reason) — not a silent removal
All outputs (library size table/plot, PCA plot, distance heatmap, verdict text) saved as reviewable artifacts

plan.title: AD lesional vs control: sample structure QC
plan.analytical_narrative: Before any differential expression testing, this plan characterizes the structure of the 12-sample atopic dermatitis dataset (6 lesional vs 6 control, single batch, unpaired, raw Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes). One step: import the raw count matrix and metadata, compute library sizes per sample, apply DESeq2's blind variance-stabilizing transformation (independent of the condition/group design, appropriate for unbiased exploratory QC), run PCA on the top 500 most variable genes, compute Euclidean sample-to-sample distances and render them as a heatmap, and specifically evaluate sample_01 (flagged in the data profile as having a library size ~4x below the median) against its group on every one of these views. Per grounded QC guidance (R-0008/R-0033), sample_01 is not dropped by default — it is kept through this QC, its library size and detected-gene count are reported explicitly beside the other 11 samples, and its position on the PCA and distance heatmap is used to render a verdict (does it cluster with its condition group, does it appear as an outlier on PC1/PC2, does it sit apart in the distance heatmap) with a stated reason for any recommendation to include/exclude it from downstream DE testing. This deliberately stops at QC — no differential expression or enrichment is run, per the research question's explicit scope.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA + sample-distance heatmap + library size barplot
